note: Links point at channels, shows and search pages rather than individual video IDs. Individual videos get deleted or renamed; channels and scoped searches do not, so these stay working for the length of the course.

alexa.name: Learn French With Alexa
alexa.why: Classroom-style lessons in English with French examples. The clearest starting point for pronunciation, verbs and numbers when you have zero French.

pieceoffrench.name: Piece of French
pieceoffrench.why: Elsa speaks slowly and precisely about daily life in France. Short stories and vlogs — the natural, lifestyle register you asked for, at a level you can actually follow.

easyfrench.name: Easy French
easyfrench.why: Street interviews in Paris with simultaneous French + English subtitles. Watch each clip twice: once with both subtitles, once with French only.

coffeebreak.name: Coffee Break French
coffeebreak.why: Season 1 genuinely starts from zero, with a teacher explaining in English. Best structured audio course for the first half of this plan.

duolingopod.name: Duolingo French Podcast
duolingopod.why: Real stories, alternating an English narrator with a French speaker. The series has ended but the full archive and transcripts remain free.

slowfrench.name: LanguaTalk Slow French
slowfrench.why: Gaëlle speaks deliberately slowly, with interactive transcripts. Your bridge from A2 into real-speed French.

rfifacile.name: Journal en français facile (RFI)
rfifacile.why: A real daily news bulletin read in deliberately simplified French, Monday to Friday, with transcripts and exercises. This is the finish line for the course.

innerfrench.name: InnerFrench
innerfrench.why: Above this course's level — bookmark it as your target for early 2027, not for now.

lesechos.name: Les Échos — Tech & Médias
lesechos.why: France's business daily. Skim headlines only early on — you are mining vocabulary, not reading for comprehension.

lemondepixels.name: Le Monde — Pixels
lemondepixels.why: Digital culture and tech coverage. Headlines and subheadings are realistic targets at A2.

zdnetfr.name: 01net
zdnetfr.why: Consumer tech news in French — shorter sentences than Le Monde, lots of shared English loanwords to anchor on.

1.focus: Alphabet, greetings, the sound of the language. Do not worry about understanding whole sentences yet.

2.focus: Office and computing words. Many are near-identical to English — collect those wins.

3.focus: Numbers and times. Replay the 70/80/90 section until the arithmetic stops surprising you.

4.focus: Daily-routine vlogs. First week where you follow a real person speaking, not a lesson.

5.focus: Shopping and money. Start skimming 01net headlines for tech vocabulary.

6.focus: Stories told in the past tense — exactly the passé composé you are learning.

7.focus: First Easy French street interviews. Expect to catch 30% — that is the correct amount.

8.focus: Professional register. Skim Les Échos headlines for business vocabulary.

9.focus: People describing how things used to be — the imparfait in the wild.

10.focus: Opinions and comparisons. Listen for 'je trouve que', 'par rapport à', 'en revanche'.

11.focus: Conversational exchanges. Start sampling RFI's news bulletin even if it is still fast.

12.focus: Real news in simplified French, every weekday. If you can follow the headlines, you have reached A2 listening.
